data.name: Sang-Froid - Tales of Werewolves
data.detailed_description:
LEGENDS OF THE ROUND TABLE

Dive into the world of King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table in our upcoming game, Legends of the Round Table!

Wishlist now on Steam.


Acerca do jogo

Combining action and strategy in a unique way, Sang-Froid: Tales of Werewolves transports you into an epic folktale co-written with best-selling Canadian author Bryan Perro (Amos Daragon, Wariwulf), in which two feuding brothers will have to put aside their differences to save their sister, who is pursued by the Devil himself!

This time however, sheer brute strength won't be enough to save the day as your enemies are way stronger than you are. Only your wits and the ability to combine ingenious traps to setup deadly ambushes will give you a chance to see the sun rise again on your frozen piece of forest...

Key Features

  • Plan your strategy! – Take advantage of the calm during the day to fill your forest with all kinds of traps that are as inventive as they are deadly.
  • Hunt your enemies! – When night falls, use the wind and lure the diabolic beasts into your traps using bait... But watch out! You have to be on constant guard to make sure you don't become the prey of the beasts you are tracking!
  • Fight heroically! – If some of the beasts get past your traps, that's when it gets bloody! First you can shoot them with your trusty musket and then eliminate the ones that survive by slaughtering them with your axe! Action and carnage guaranteed!
  • Use fear to your advantage! – All the mechanics of the game revolve around the innovative concept of Fear Factor, which makes your ability to intimidate your enemy your best weapon. For example, use fire to frighten the wolves and scatter their packs.
  • Customize your character! – Choose one of the two O'Carroll brothers and develop your character using a skill system based on role-playing games (RPGs), making your hero as unique as he is powerful!
  • Discover a rich universe! – Immerse yourself in 19th century Canada where legends meet History in a world filled with lore and wonders. Buy historical weapons and items, fight mythical beasts and uncover the truth about werewolves...

reviews.review:
Sang Froid Tales of Werewolves is a game I did not really know what to expect from at first, because it mixes together a few things that normally would not be put in the same game. I am playing as one of two brothers in 19th century Canada, trying to protect my sister from werewolves and other creatures while also dealing with the Devil. During the day I get time to prepare the forest, place traps and decide how I want the coming night to play out. When night arrives, the game turns into a much more active fight where I have to hunt the creatures and deal with anything that gets through my setup. That combination is what makes it stand out to me.

The trap system is easily my favourite part. I am not simply waiting for enemies to appear and then attacking them. I can place different traps around the forest, use bait to lure enemies towards them and take advantage of the way they move through the area. I also have to think about fear, which can be used to scare enemies and change how they behave. I really like having this planning stage because it makes me feel like I am preparing an actual hunt rather than just walking into another fight. When a setup works exactly how I planned, it is much more satisfying than simply defeating something with a weapon.

The action side is simpler, but I still think it works well alongside the strategy. If a creature gets through my traps, I can use a musket to weaken it before getting closer and finishing the fight with an axe. The different enemies also make me think about how I prepare the area, rather than allowing me to rely on one trap for everything. There is a proper sense of danger because the creatures are stronger than I am, so going into a fight without preparing properly can end badly. I like that the game encourages me to use my brain first and my weapons second.

I also like the setting more than I expected. The snowy Canadian wilderness, old weapons and folklore give the game a really strong atmosphere, and the story is based around a folktale style adventure rather than a standard modern werewolf story. The two brothers have different personalities and I can choose between them while developing my character through an RPG style skill system. There is also a decent amount of lore behind the world, which gives the campaign more personality than I expected from what is basically a strategy game with werewolves in it.

The biggest problem for me is that the game can be awkward in places. It came out in 2013, and I can feel its age in the graphics, interface and some of the controls. The combat is also not nearly as satisfying as the trap planning. When I am setting everything up during the day, I feel like I have a lot of freedom. Once the fighting starts, some of that freedom disappears and the action can feel clunky compared with newer games. I also have to spend some time learning how the different systems work before the game really starts making sense, so it is not something I would recommend if I just wanted a simple action game.

The progression helps keep the campaign moving forward. I can improve my chosen brother through skills and purchase historical weapons and other equipment, so there is always something to work towards. I like that my upgrades actually support the way I want to play rather than completely replacing the strategy. At the same time, I think the game sometimes makes me work a little too hard to get the most out of its systems. There are moments where I know what I want to do but the older controls or interface make it harder than it should be. That does not ruin the experience for me, but it stops it from feeling as polished as the idea deserves.

Overall, Sang Froid is one of those games I appreciate because there is not really anything else quite like it. The combination of trap planning, hunting, fear mechanics and direct combat gives me a reason to think before every night, and the Canadian folklore setting gives the whole thing a lot of character. The older presentation and occasionally awkward combat hold it back, but the main strategy system is strong enough that I can look past a lot of those problems. I would not call it perfect, but I think it is a genuinely creative game that does enough differently to be worth playing, especially if I enjoy strategy games that let me get involved in the action myself.

Rating: 8.2/10
